target.title: fix(mcp): suppress unhandled rejection from async gateway event handler
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `onEvent` callback in `OpenClawChannelBridge` calls `void this.handleGatewayEvent(event)` without a `.catch()` handler. Since `handleGatewayEvent` is async and can reject, this creates an unhandled promise rejection that crashes the MCP gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a noop `.catch(() => {})` to suppress the unhandled rejection, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase for fire-and-forget async callbacks.

## User Impact

Prevents the gateway from crashing when an MCP channel bridge event handler throws.

## Evidence

### Behavior
The `onEvent` callback now attaches a `.catch(() => {})` to the fire-and-forget `handleGatewayEvent(event)` promise.

### Source
`src/mcp/channel-bridge.ts:151`
```ts
onEvent: (event) => {
  void this.handleGatewayEvent(event).catch(() => {});
},
```

### Test output
```
$ pnpm test -- src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts
 ✓ |unit| src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts (16 tests) 312ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Duration  1.83s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 14.16s
```

### Notes
- This is a defensive fix; the callback is fire-and-forget by design.
- The `.catch(() => {})` pattern is already used elsewhere for similar fire-and-forget handlers.
- Existing tests continue to pass.
